human-population-s3.passage: Placeholder passage in our own words: people multiply faster than farms can grow food, so hunger will check every growing population unless births fall.

items.q: Placeholder: what does a crude birth rate of 20 mean?
options: 20 births a year per 100 people over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: crude rates are per 1,000 people per year.
options: Right: the rate is per 1,000 people.
Per 100 would be a percent, not a crude rate.
Children per woman is a fertility rate.
Growth is births minus deaths, in percent.

items.q: Placeholder: a country has a crude birth rate of 30 and a crude death rate of 10. What is its rate of natural increase?

mistakes.why: Placeholder: 20 is the difference per 1,000 people. Divide by 10 to turn it into a percent.
Placeholder: you divided by 100. Crude rates are per 1,000, so divide the difference by 10.

items.q: Placeholder: the population grows 2% a year. Write the setup for its doubling time, then the answer.

why.correct: Placeholder: by the rule of 70, $\frac{70}{2} = 35$ years.

mistakes.why: Placeholder: the rule of 70 puts 70 on top: 70 divided by the growth rate.
Placeholder: use the rate in percent (2), not as a decimal (0.02).
Placeholder: that is the year it doubles; the question asks how many years.

items.q: Placeholder: a population of 40 million in 2020 grows 2% a year. In what year does it reach 80 million?

mistakes.why: Placeholder: 35 is the doubling time. Add it to the start year to get the year.

items.q: Placeholder: a city grew from 120 thousand to 150 thousand people. Write the setup for the percent change, then the answer.

mistakes.why: Placeholder: divide by the old value (120), not the new one.
Placeholder: multiply by 100 to turn the fraction into a percent.
Placeholder: that is the change from 150 back to 120. Start from the old value.

items.q: Placeholder: which country in the table grows fastest from births and deaths?
options: Country B over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: country A has the largest gap: $35 - 10 = 25$ per 1,000.
options: Right: 32 minus 8 is the largest gap.
Country D's death rate is higher than its birth rate.

items.q: Placeholder: what is country B's rate of natural increase?

mistakes.why: Placeholder: 11 is per 1,000 people. Divide by 10 for a percent.

items.q: Placeholder: which countries have a birth rate at least ten above their death rate? Select all that apply.

why.correct: Placeholder: a country grows when its birth rate is above its death rate.
options: Its death rate is above its birth rate.

items.q: Placeholder: what does the wide base of this pyramid show?
options: Many children compared with older people
Many older people compared with children over the same years
Equal numbers in each age group

why.correct: Placeholder: a wide base means a large young cohort.
options: Right: the bars for children are longest.
The bars for older people are short.
The bars are not the same length.

items.q: Placeholder: if birth rates stay high, what happens to this population in 20 years?
options: It grows, as the young cohort has children
It shrinks, as the young cohort ages over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: the large young cohort reaches child-bearing age.
options: A large young cohort means growth, not decline.

items.q: Placeholder: which policy would slow this population's growth most?
options: Raising the death rate over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: education and work for women lower fertility.
options: Right: more schooling for women lowers fertility.
Roads do not change fertility directly.
No policy aims to raise deaths.
Immigration is not the driver here.

items.q: Placeholder: what is the author's claim?
options: Food keeps up with people over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: the passage argues people grow faster than food.
options: The passage is not about cities.
The passage does not say that.

items.q: Placeholder: what does the author assume?
options: Food grows more slowly than people
Food grows faster than people over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: the claim rests on food growing slowly.
options: Right: the assumption behind the claim.
The passage does not assume falling births.
The passage does not say that.

items.q: Placeholder: which evidence would weaken the claim?
options: Crop yields that rose faster than population
A drought in one year over the same years

why.correct: Placeholder: yields rising faster than people would refute it.
options: One drought does not test the long-run claim.
City size is not evidence about food.

items.q: Placeholder: explain why country A's population will keep growing even if its birth rate falls.

why.correct: Placeholder: a large young cohort will have children for years.

specific.model: Placeholder: because country A has a large cohort of young people, the number of births will increase as they reach child-bearing age, so the population keeps growing for decades.

why.1: Placeholder: a high death rate slows growth.
why.2: Placeholder: the question is about births.
why.3: Placeholder: a small cohort would slow growth.

Add the doubling time to the start year
